Welcome

At Dummy Mock Test Inc., our people are our most important investment. This guide summarizes the benefits available to you and your family, explains how to enroll, and shows where to get help. Our program is designed to be competitive with large employers, giving you choice, financial protection and support for your health, wealth and wellbeing.

1. Eligibility and Enrollment
Who is eligible
Employees: regular full-time employees scheduled for 30+ hours per week. Part-time employees scheduled 20-29 hours are eligible for 401(k), EAP and selected voluntary benefits.
Dependents: legal spouse or registered domestic partner; children up to age 26 regardless of student or marital status; disabled children of any age who meet plan criteria.
Coverage start: the first day of the month following your date of hire (or on your date of hire if hired on the 1st).
When you can enroll
As a new hire: within 31 days of your start date.
Annual open enrollment: each November for coverage effective January 1.
Qualifying life event: within 31 days of the event (60 days for birth or adoption). See Section 10.
How to enroll
Log in to the benefits portal (Workday or equivalent HRIS) and select Benefits > Enroll.
Review plan options, add dependents and upload verification documents.
Name beneficiaries for life insurance and 401(k).
Submit and save your confirmation statement.
2. Medical Plans
Choose from three national medical plans administered by a major carrier. All plans cover in-network preventive care at 100%, include prescription drug coverage, and offer virtual care visits.
Subject to IRS rules for HSA-eligible plans. ** Preventive generics on the IRS preventive list are covered at 100%.
Your cost per paycheck (26 pay periods)
Dummy Mock Test Inc. pays about 80% of total premiums on average. Rates below are illustrative.
Medical plan features
Spousal surcharge: $50 per paycheck if your spouse has access to medical coverage through their own employer.
Tobacco-free incentive: save $25 per paycheck by completing the tobacco-free attestation or a cessation program.
Care navigation: a concierge advocate helps you find providers, resolve claims and get second opinions.
Centers of excellence: enhanced coverage for joint replacement, spine, cancer and bariatric care.
Fertility and family-building: up to a $20,000 lifetime benefit for IVF, egg freezing, adoption and surrogacy.

blocks.text: Optional coverage above guaranteed-issue amounts ($500,000 employee; $50,000 spouse) requires an Evidence of Insurability form. Life insurance includes travel assistance, will preparation and grief counseling at no cost.
6. Retirement Savings: 401(k)
Eligibility: immediate, from your first paycheck.
Auto-enrollment: new hires are enrolled at 6% pre-tax, increasing 1% each year up to 10%, unless you opt out.
Company match: 100% of the first 4% you contribute, plus 50% of the next 2% (up to 5% total).
Vesting: your contributions are always 100% vested. Company match vests 100% after 2 years of service.
Options: pre-tax, Roth and after-tax contributions, with catch-up contributions at age 50+.
Investments: target-date funds (default), index funds and a self-directed brokerage window.
Financial wellness: free one-on-one planning sessions and online tools through the recordkeeper.
Example: earn $90,000 and contribute 6% ($5,400). The company adds $4,500, for a total of $9,900 per year.
Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
If your company is publicly traded, an ESPP lets you buy company stock at a 15% discount through payroll deductions, in six-month offering periods. Remove this section if it doesn't apply.

blocks.text: 8. Wellbeing and Support Programs
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): free, confidential, 24/7. Includes 8 free counseling sessions per issue for you and your household, plus legal and financial consultations.
Mental health app and therapy network: on-demand therapy and coaching, with low or no copays.
Wellness rewards: earn up to $400 per year (HSA deposit or gift card) for a biometric screening, annual physical and activity challenges.
Fitness: $50 per month toward gym memberships or fitness subscriptions.
Chronic condition programs: diabetes, hypertension and musculoskeletal (virtual physical therapy) at no cost.
Caregiving support: 10 days of subsidized backup child or elder care per year, plus help finding care.
Family planning and maternity support: a dedicated care team from preconception to return-to-work.

10. Life Events, COBRA and Changes

Outside open enrollment, you can change elections only after a qualifying life event, and the change must be consistent with the event. Report changes within 31 days (60 days for birth or adoption, or for gaining or losing Medicaid/CHIP).

rows: Add spouse/partner and their children; change plans
Add child; increase FSA or life insurance
Gain or lose eligibility; change elections
Move out of plan service area
Change medical plan (for example, from EPO to PPO)

blocks.text: COBRA continuation

If coverage ends because of termination, reduced hours, or a dependent losing eligibility, you and your covered dependents may continue medical, dental, vision and Health Care FSA coverage for up to 18 months (36 months in some cases). You pay the full premium plus a 2% administrative fee. A COBRA notice is mailed to your home address.

12. Required Notices and Glossary
Annual notices
U.S. employers of this size must provide several notices each year. They are available on the benefits portal, and paper copies are free on request:
Medicare Part D Creditable Coverage Notice
HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices and Special Enrollment Rights
Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act (WHCRA) Notice
Newborns' and Mothers' Health Protection Act Notice
Premium Assistance under Medicaid and CHIP (CHIPRA) Notice
Summary of Benefits and Coverage (SBC) for each medical plan
Summary Plan Descriptions (SPDs) and ERISA rights
ACA Marketplace coverage notice and Form 1095-C (issued each January)
No Surprises Act and Transparency in Coverage disclosures
